label: Education

identity.owner_line: The owner is an educator who wears many hats: teacher, trainer, consultant, creator, community host.
identity.founding_frame: You're not installing software. You're setting up an AI-native education business - one person wearing many hats, backed by an AI staff that remembers everything and does real work. I'm your chief of staff: I run the office, route the work, and protect you from mistakes.
identity.q1: What's your education business? What do you teach, train, consult on, or create?
identity.q1_pushback: Say it the way you'd say it to someone about to pay you.
identity.q2_examples: courses, coaching, workshops, a membership, consulting, done-for-you work

_managers_notes: DEFAULTS ONLY. A local {dept}/manager.json OVERRIDES this entry wholesale. Pack declares, owner disposes.
Every cadence ships enabled:false. Founding does not switch on recurring spend the owner has not agreed to; /campus-doctor and the onboarding ladder offer them later.
Every gate ships draft or darker, and buyer_defaults.all_surfaces is 'draft' on all four - enforced as an ERROR by tools/lint_managers.py, not left to good intentions.

dept_dir and state_file assume the 'departments' filing structure because that is the founding default. A clients or projects campus has NO department folders and still has all four managers - the staff org is independent of how finished work is filed. campus-start resolves the real paths and writes them literally into the local manager.json.

Consumers ENUMERATE the managers that exist and read each contract. Never hardcode these four ids, never assume dept_dir == id + '/', and never derive state_file - it is a literal declared path. Deriving it would have broken the first campus this ran on, whose folders are named '{dept}-manager/'.

The shape enum is CLOSED: calendar | pipeline | roster | hybrid. Shapes describe HOW STATE MOVES, not what business the pack serves. A consulting pack can declare desks called Studio and Bench and reuse these four shapes unchanged. A fifth shape is a kernel change and a version bump.

wiki_taxonomy.what: One page per client, student, member, or partner. Their context, history, patterns, what has worked and what has not.
The owner's methodology, frameworks, teaching concepts, business principles. Their IP — the thinking that defines their work.
One page per product, program, or service AS SOLD. Positioning, pricing history, what converted, how it evolved.
Major business decisions and their rationale. Implications longer than 6 months — strategy calls, pivots, pricing changes.
Competitor observations, market trends, audience insights, industry shifts, signals from other operators in the space.
Systems, tools, workflows, processes the business runs on. How things actually get done.
Multi-session initiatives with history — builds, plugins, launches, migrations. The WORK of making a thing, as distinct from the thing once it is sold.
Significant one-time analyses worth preserving — research findings, audits, teardowns, validated data.
One rolling page per department. Purpose, active work, observed patterns. Updated in place, never duplicated.

_wiki_taxonomy_notes: This list is FIXED at runtime. The agent picks one of these per page and never invents a category.
A niche with a different shape declares its own list here; the kernel has no taxonomy of its own beyond a fallback.

Precedence when two fit: decisions > concepts (the call, then the reusable framework it produced); offers > projects (once it is for sale, the offer page is canonical and the project page becomes build history); operations > projects (a standing system, not a one-time build).
